replies.author: 0xC0DED0D0
replies.text:
Looks pretty neat! Maybe not for me personally, but I like the idea. 👍

There's clearly a parental control angle here also. Much better "my first (dumb) smartphone" solution than the ubiquitous iPhone, for sure.

Once the codebase is mature enough (is it already?) I wouldn't mind seeing this being integrated within GrapheneOS, as a setup toggle, not requiring ADB.

Security and privacy (in that order) remains GrapheneOS' focus, but on that second point – "dumbing down" a smartphone is certainly within the scope of increasing privacy. Escaping the addicting algorithms and control, as you've rightly pointed out.

replies.author: flourishdev
replies.text:
0xC0DED0D0 Thank you!

0xC0DED0D0 Once the codebase is mature enough (is it already?)

There's no bugs (tm) that I've encountered but I will update it if there's any found. I don't have any more features planned besides compatibility with QR code provisioning (I would have to look into it). I'm running it on my main phone so I'll definitely fix anything I find. It relies on the device management APIs already in Android, Odysseus (and other device policy controllers / MDM apps) just let you use them.

0xC0DED0D0 I wouldn't mind seeing this being integrated within GrapheneOS, as a setup toggle, not requiring ADB.

Once this issue is solved and this PR (or similar) are merged, then ADB-less setup should be possible. How it would work is that you'd scan a QR code during the initial setup (after install or factory reset) and Odysseus would be downloaded and made the device owner.

One thing I plan to do is open issues for apps that allow full browser access through the WebView because it's recommended against by Android and it allows people using Odysseus or similar to bypass the restrictions they intend.

So far the apps I've found that do this are:

Street complete, CakeWallet/Monero.com, all Ente apps.

So I had to remove them from my user profile until it gets fixed (if ever).

replies.author: flourishdev
replies.text:
0xC0DED0D0 There's clearly a parental control angle here also

Yeah I imagine it would work well as managed by a parent (or friend/family member) because you wouldn't have to worry about the owner profile password management–they could just unlock it for you after a restart.

It seems to me that MDM type solutions are the only effective parental control there is, at least on GrapheneOS and iOS. iOS 27 may have made the built in screentime good enough, but Apple Configurator (Apple's MDM) worked great up until then and may still be better.

replies.author: flourishdev
replies.text:
I'm making a second version of the app that will also work on stock Pixels (because they don't have improved user profiles that GrapheneOS adds) and only uses the Owner profile.

This has benefits in that you don't have to worry about protecting the owner's password so you can restart and update GrapheneOS without worrying about learning the password that restricts your setup or typing it again. It will allow you to update your apps without being able to install new ones without the password. Also apps that only work in owner proifle.

The downside is it needs the list all apps permission and it's a bit more complex.

Anyone have name suggestions?

I was thinking like:

• Odysseus Solo

• Odysseus Owner

• Odysseus Android

But none of them really feel like they're ideal.

replies.author: flourishdev
replies.text:
I decided on Beeswax for the name. It works as an owner only setup and should work on Stock which I'll test later. It is a rather elegant setup and simpler setup than Odysseus.

It hides browsers when locked instead of not installing them. It hides newly installed apps allowing you full access to app stores even when locked so you can update your apps without being able to use new apps without your unlock code.

The advantages of Odysseus is it requires no permissions and it allows user profiles to be used. That second part may be added as a feature to Beeswax. Another feature I was thinking of is the ability to hide (block) apps on command because currently the only way to block an app is for it to be installed while Beeswax is locked.

https://github.com/flourish-today/Beeswax

replies.author: Novaliss
replies.text:
flourishdev decided on Beeswax for the name

Very good name for the app.👍

replies.author: flourishdev
replies.text:
Beeswax turned out to be just better in pretty much every way than Odysseus. I mean, Odysseus is fully functional, but it has downsides for user experience with the owner password, app updates, and phone restarts. Odysseus also only worked on GrapheneOS because it relied on improved user profiles.

Beeswax solves those issues—I guess you could say beeswax is the bees knees :)

I made a website for it: https://beeswax.getflourish.org

So I'm moving Odysseus to "maintenance mode", not that it would've gotten many more features, but Beeswax will get more features.

I haven't actually moved my main phone over to Beeswax yet, but I will, and then, after a few weeks of regular use, I'll do a stable release. I'm gonna be writing down the lock code on paper as my method.

replies.author: flourishdev
replies.text:
I transferred all my data, deleted the user profile, deactivated and uninstalled Odysseus, and activated Beeswax.

This is the first time I'll really have been using GrapheneOS with just the Owner profile and I'm liking it so far. There's two bugs I can think of off the top of my head which only happen in the user profile that don't in the owner.

It was somewhat nice with Odysseus to not have the extra app stores just visually in my app dock there's a lot more, but functionally it's the same result but also way better. It just makes way more sense to have a separate code that protects the setup rather than the whole owner profile.

I'm glad no really important apps allow full browser access within themselves. The most detrimental one for me is Ente so I really should submit an issue.

replies.author: swerolukini
replies.text:
what about factory reset? that solves the problem of not having a browser. And if it is about distractions then sometimes that little friction isn't enough to stop a user.

also i have termux for backup script and it can do pm install-existing to recover the package, even if 'uninstall' the system apps.

the only solution for on-device prevention is a custom graphene build that starts with no browser (but keep WebView to not break things) and no app store, both of which should be fine to remove. Then when setting up after flashing, you can temporarily install these apps and then remove them once you have the stuff you need. No way to recover them on-device.

thoughts? building custom requires specs i don't have.

edit: I see Beeswax addresses "connecting with ADB won't get you around it. Only the lock code or a factory reset get through." You can't uninstall with adb? But yeah, factory reset does occur to bypass.

replies.author: flourishdev
replies.text:
swerolukini Yes, factory reset is the only option to browse and access new apps if you lose/don't have the code.

Personally I consider a factory reset enough friction to prevent someone from bypassing it, but perhaps someone with little data on the device may not feel that way. Someone with a good backup system, even though that's totally recommended, may be making this have less friction.

I could add factory reset prevention from the UI. Afaict it's still possible through the recovery mode so this feature would rely on security through obscurity. It could work in the sense that someone who only used this managed device without a browser or information source would likely know how to factory reset from UI, but wouldn't intuitively know how to reset from recovery mode without instructions.

swerolukini the only solution for on-device prevention is a custom graphene build that starts with no browser (but keep WebView to not break things) and no app store, both of which should be fine to remove. Then when setting up after flashing, you can temporarily install these apps and then remove them once you have the stuff you need. No way to recover them on-device.

It would be better probably if you could modify it to not allow factory resets without a code or at all. I looked it up and some OSes either have factory reset protection which would prevent access after the factory reset occurred. Apparently Samsung Knox can specifically deny factory resets in both Android Settings and the Recovery Mode.

swerolukini thoughts? building custom requires specs i don't have.

Me neither, and I imagine it would be a ton of work to keep up on updates. I'm also not super interested in it. If Android provided a way, I would add it as a toggle, likely.
